title: How Ghana Growers Works
excerpt: A simple guide to how farmers, buyers, suppliers, and partners use Ghana Growers.
keyPoints: Farmers, buyers, and suppliers use one trusted agriculture network.
Clear records make it easier for Ghana Growers to follow up.
Verified information helps reduce confusion before trade.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: Ghana Growers connects farmers, suppliers, buyers, and partners across Ghana. The platform helps people find produce, request supply, join the network, learn practical farming steps, and use GG FarmMate for daily farm decisions.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Check that your farm, business, product, region, district, phone number, and WhatsApp details are clear before submitting information. Good records help Ghana Growers understand what you offer or need.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Start with the page that matches your goal. Use Buy to source produce or inputs, Sell to join as a seller, Directory to find farmers or suppliers, and GG FarmMate when you need farming guidance.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: Use GG FarmMate when you have a farm question, need a practical next step, or want help checking a crop problem. Use Crop Doctor when a clear photo can reduce guessing.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Choose Buy, Sell, Directory, or GG FarmMate based on what you need today.

title: How to Use GG FarmMate
excerpt: Learn how to ask questions, use FarmMate tools, and get practical next steps.
keyPoints: Ask one clear farm question at a time.
Mention the crop and what you can see.
Follow the next step before adding more details.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: GG FarmMate helps farmers make better farming decisions every day. It can guide crop checks, spraying decisions, planting questions, and practical next steps using local FarmMate knowledge.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Before asking, note the crop, growth stage, visible signs, recent rain, and where the problem appears. A clear question helps FarmMate avoid guessing.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Ask one short question such as: My maize leaves are yellow. What should I check first? If FarmMate asks a follow-up question, answer it directly.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: Use Ask FarmMate for questions. Use Crop Doctor when a photo would help, especially for leaf spots, curling leaves, wilting, pest damage, or an unknown crop problem.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Open GG FarmMate and ask one practical question about your farm today.

title: How to Use Crop Doctor
excerpt: Learn how to upload a clear crop photo so FarmMate can avoid guessing.
keyPoints: Use bright natural light.
Show the affected part clearly.
Treat results as guidance, not a final diagnosis.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: Crop Doctor checks a crop photo and gives practical guidance. It cannot guarantee a diagnosis, but it can help you decide what to inspect next.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Take a clear photo of the affected leaves, stem, fruit, or whole plant. Avoid blurry photos, heavy shadows, and photos taken too far away.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Upload one clear image. Read the possible issue, visible signs, recommended action, prevention, and next best action before applying any treatment.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: Use Crop Doctor for visible crop problems. Use Ask FarmMate after the result if you need help deciding what to check next.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Take one clear crop photo in good light and upload it to Crop Doctor.

title: How to Prepare Your Harvest Before Selling
excerpt: Simple checks for sorting, packaging, quantity, and buyer readiness.
keyPoints: Sort damaged produce before estimating quantity.
Prepare packaging and pickup details early.
Be clear about quality, quantity, and timing.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: Good harvest preparation helps farmers speak clearly with buyers. Sorting, packaging, and quantity checks reduce confusion before pickup or delivery.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Check damaged produce, size differences, packaging needs, expected quantity, harvest date, pickup location, and whether delivery is possible.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Sort damaged produce first. Estimate quantity using a clear unit such as crates, sacks, bunches, kilograms, or bags. Keep photos ready if Ghana Growers asks for them.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: Use GG FarmMate if crop quality problems appear before selling. Use Crop Doctor if spots, wilting, or pest signs are affecting the harvest.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Sort your harvest and write down quantity, location, and preferred pickup time.

title: Maize Leaves Turning Yellow: What to Check First
excerpt: A simple field guide for farmers who notice yellowing maize leaves.
keyPoints: Check whether older or newer leaves yellow first.
Look at soil moisture and drainage.
Use Crop Doctor if a photo would reduce guessing.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: Yellow maize leaves can come from nutrient stress, poor water conditions, root problems, pests, or disease. Do not jump to disease before checking the pattern.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Check if the yellowing starts on older leaves, newer leaves, or the whole plant. Look at drainage, soil moisture, spacing, roots, and pest damage.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Inspect five nearby maize plants. If older leaves are pale yellow and the field is not waterlogged, nutrient stress may be possible. Improve field observation before applying chemicals.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: Ask FarmMate if you can describe where the yellowing starts. Use Crop Doctor if the leaves have spots, curling, insect damage, or unclear symptoms.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Check five plants and note whether the yellowing starts on old leaves, new leaves, or everywhere.

title: Tomato Production: Field Checks Before Flowering
excerpt: Practical checks for tomato farmers before flowering and fruiting begin.
keyPoints: Check drainage after rain.
Look under leaves early.
Support plants before heavy fruiting.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: Tomato plants need steady checks before flowering. Early field checks can reduce losses from water stress, pests, poor airflow, and weak plant support.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Check drainage, leaf colour, leaf spots, pest signs under leaves, plant spacing, airflow, and whether plants need staking before fruiting.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Clear blocked drains, remove weeds around plants, inspect lower leaves, and support weak plants early. Avoid spraying until the problem is confirmed.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: Ask FarmMate about watering, flowering, or field checks. Use Crop Doctor if tomato leaves show spots, curling, yellowing, or unusual damage.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Check the lower leaves and drainage before the next rain.

title: Cassava Leaves Curling: What to Check
excerpt: Simple checks for curling cassava leaves before assuming disease.
keyPoints: Check young leaves and older leaves separately.
Look for insects before assuming disease.
Ask for help if curling spreads quickly.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: Cassava leaf curling can be linked to pest pressure, disease, heat stress, nutrient stress, or young leaf growth. Check carefully before deciding what to do.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Look at whether curling is on young leaves, older leaves, or the whole plant. Check under leaves for insects and compare affected plants with healthy nearby plants.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Inspect several plants across the field. Remove badly affected leaves only if advised locally, keep the field clean, and avoid chemical treatment without confirmation.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: Use Crop Doctor if a clear photo can show the curling pattern. Contact an extension officer if symptoms spread quickly across many plants.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Take a clear photo of one affected leaf and one whole plant, then use Crop Doctor.

title: Before You Spray: 3 Things to Check
excerpt: Check weather, wind, and the real crop problem before spraying.
keyPoints: Check rain before spraying.
Avoid strong wind.
Confirm the pest or disease first.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: Spraying at the wrong time can waste money and may not help the crop. Check weather, wind, and the actual problem before spraying.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Check if rain is expected, whether wind is strong, and whether the crop problem is pest, disease, nutrient stress, or water stress.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Delay spraying if rain is likely soon or wind is strong. Confirm the problem first. Follow the product label carefully if a chemical is truly needed.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: Ask FarmMate: Can I spray today? Use Crop Doctor when the problem on the plant is unclear.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Check rain and wind before mixing any spray.

title: Rainy Season Farm Checklist
excerpt: Prepare fields, drainage, seed, and labour before heavy rains.
keyPoints: Clear drainage paths.
Check seed and tools early.
Avoid planting in waterlogged soil.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: Rainy season work becomes easier when drainage, seed, tools, and labour are prepared before heavy rains arrive.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Check blocked drainage, seed condition, tool readiness, field access, labour availability, and low areas that hold water.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Clear drainage paths, keep seed dry, prepare tools, and avoid planting in waterlogged soil. Use mulch where it helps protect young plants.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: Ask FarmMate before planting, spraying, or harvesting around rain. Use Crop Doctor if wet weather is followed by leaf spots or wilting.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Walk the field and clear the main drainage paths today.

title: How Buyers Source Produce Through Ghana Growers
excerpt: How buyers find farmers, browse listings, submit demand, and request connections.
audience: Buyers, processors, traders, restaurants, and institutions
keyPoints: Browse before submitting a request.
Use clear quantity and timing details.
Confirm quality, packaging, and transport before buying.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: Buyers can use Ghana Growers to discover farmers, check supply, and request help when produce or inputs are not easy to find.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Check product name, preferred region, quantity, delivery date, quality requirements, packaging, and pickup or delivery needs.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Search Buy first. If you cannot find what you need, submit a clear request so Ghana Growers can help source produce or suppliers.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: FarmMate is for farming guidance. Use Buy or Contact for sourcing produce, inputs, or suppliers.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Write down product, quantity, region, and deadline before requesting help.

title: Become a Supplier Guide
excerpt: What agricultural suppliers should prepare before joining Ghana Growers.
audience: Input dealers, logistics providers, packaging companies, consultants, and service providers
keyPoints: Share your supplier category clearly.
List the regions or districts you serve.
Use simple product and service descriptions.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: Suppliers can join Ghana Growers to make seeds, fertilizer, tools, equipment, logistics, packaging, and agricultural services easier to discover.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Prepare your business name, contact person, WhatsApp number, supplier category, service area, products or services, and any useful images or logo.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Describe your offer in simple words. Mention where you operate and what farmers, buyers, or partners can request from you.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: Use FarmMate for farming guidance. Use supplier registration when you want Ghana Growers users to discover your products or services.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Prepare your supplier category, coverage area, and WhatsApp contact before joining.

title: Simple Records for Small Poultry Flocks
excerpt: Record keeping that helps poultry keepers track feed, mortality, eggs, and sales.
keyPoints: Track feed purchases and daily use.
Record eggs, losses, and sales.
Use records before buying more feed or birds.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: Simple poultry records help farmers understand costs, egg production, bird losses, and sales. A notebook is enough to begin.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Check feed use, water intake, egg numbers, bird losses, medicine use, sales, and changes in bird behaviour.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Write the date, feed used, eggs collected, birds lost, medicine used, and sales each day. Review the notes every week.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: FarmMate is focused on farming decisions. For serious animal health problems, contact a qualified veterinary or extension officer.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Start one daily poultry record page today.

title: Starting a Backyard Vegetable Garden
excerpt: A practical guide for growing vegetables at home with limited space.
keyPoints: Start small.
Choose a sunny place with water access.
Check plants often.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: A small backyard garden can provide fresh vegetables for the home. Start with a manageable space and crops you use often.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Check sunlight, water access, soil quality, drainage, container size, and whether the crop fits your space.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Start with a small bed or containers. Use compost or well-prepared soil. Water in the morning or late afternoon.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: Ask FarmMate for crop choice, watering, spacing, or pest checks. Use Crop Doctor if leaves start curling, yellowing, or showing spots.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Choose one sunny spot and start with two or three vegetables you cook often.

title: Video Guide: How to Use Crop Doctor
excerpt: A short video guide for farmers learning how to upload crop photos for advisory guidance.
keyPoints: Take a clear crop photo.
Read results as guidance.
Ask FarmMate what to check next.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: This video lesson will help farmers learn how to use Crop Doctor well. The page is ready for the video when the Ghana Growers training media is available.

sections.heading: What to check
sections.body: Check that the photo is clear, bright, and close enough to show the affected crop part.

sections.heading: What to do now
sections.body: Use Crop Doctor when a photo can reduce guessing. Read the result carefully and avoid treating the crop before checking the next step.

sections.heading: When to use FarmMate or Crop Doctor
sections.body: Use Crop Doctor for the photo check, then Ask FarmMate if you need help deciding what to inspect or do next.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: Open GG FarmMate and upload a clear crop photo when you see a visible crop problem.
